summary:
I finished the schema survey and wrote schema.md. It maps mirage_vmaf's JSON report at 75cf6e0 against §7 and against what §3 adds. Nothing in the worktree was changed (git status is clean). Every number comes from 14 runs saved under schema-survey/runs/, each with its exact command and full output, or from a cited file:line.

- **Report today:** mirage_vmaf has two hand-written layouts. A pair report has 23 top-level keys. A ladder report has 22 top-level keys, 14 per pair and 6 per frame. There is no JSON library or JSON reader in src/.
- **The three provenance fields:** schema_version, tool_version and git_commit are absent. The repository holds no JSON Schema file, and the build has no version. P-006 has the eval tooling record the commit.
- **Committed records:** the 167 committed reports have no version field and come in 12 mirage_vmaf layouts plus the player's. Scripts tell the layouts apart by which keys are present.
- **§7 against the report:** about half of §7's fields exist under the same name. Five exist under another name or only in part: model, model_sha256, reference_identity, ffmpeg_libraries, and ref_pts/dis_pts. The rest are absent, timeline and attributions included. The one real naming conflict: §7's `ladder` is a list, the report's `ladder` is the master playlist object.
- **Sizes:** per-frame lines are 92.46% of a ladder report at 300 frames per pair and 99.91% over every frame. The full report is 27969051 bytes of text, 1792136 as committed. Repeating every score in a timeline would make it 54462827 bytes. A session's per-segment records are 100 per variant, against 36000 frames per 60 fps pair.
- **Where the timeline goes:** there are three options with trade-offs. My recommendation (labelled as mine, the choice is the owner's) is option B: a separate document per session that names the ladder report by a hash. B differs from §7, so the difference has to be reported to the owner.

The unit tests for the report, JSON and CLI pass at 75cf6e0: 1368 assertions in 43 test cases.
key_findings: Two hand-written mirage_vmaf layouts. The pair report (vmafreport::to_json, src/VMAFReport.cpp:230-240) has 23 top-level keys. The ladder report (ladder_to_json, :242-325) has 22 top-level keys, 14 per pair and 6 per frame: index, ref_index, dis_index, ref_pts, dis_pts, vmaf (runs 04, 08). There are two other JSON writers, the player's write_json (src/VMAFAnalyzer.cpp:907-948, kept until §7's schema by D-040) and --net-report (src/NetworkLogger.cpp:1027-1067). src/ has no JSON reader (run 14); the only one is the tests' (tests/test_vmaf_report.cpp:26).

schema_version, tool_version and git_commit are absent: no such key or constant in src/, tools/ or tests/, and the repository holds no JSON Schema file (run 02). `tool` is only the name 'mirage_vmaf' (tools/mirage_vmaf.cpp:161), and CMake's project has no VERSION (CMakeLists.txt:2). P-006 has the eval tooling record the commit (docs/DECISIONS.md:791), in environment.txt or build.txt next to each record; pool_check.py itself records none (runs 12, 13). Six eval scripts version their own outputs as report_version: 1 (run 02).

The committed reports have no version and come in many layouts. There are 167 files (142 pair, 24 ladder, 1 player) in 13 groups of keys, 12 of them mirage_vmaf's. Only 8 files have every key checked (run 03). Readers tell the layouts apart by key presence (eval/consistency/vmafdelta.py:671-690, :1011).

§7 field by field. Present: libvmaf_version (plus libvmaf_package_version, D-006), reference_mode (plus 'explicit-pair', already reported as difference 2), scaler, pooled (plus 2 values) and alignment (plus 19 keys). Under another name or only in part: model_id is `model` plus `model_source`. model_path_hash is `model_sha256`, a hash of the file's contents, null for a built-in model (P-017, docs/DECISIONS.md:1027). reference_identity is a URI only; just the master playlist is hashed (src/VMAFLadder.cpp:332). ffmpeg_version is ffmpeg_libraries, five library versions (P-035). frames[].pts is ref_pts and dis_pts, raw best_effort_timestamp in seconds (P-006, docs/DECISIONS.md:786). Absent: environment, backpressure_policy, timeline, attributions, benchmark; pool and started_s/ended_s cover part of benchmark.

Naming conflict: §7's `ladder` is a list of variants, the report's `ladder` is the master playlist object (src/VMAFReport.cpp:274-281). ladder_check.py reads it as an object (:254, :349-354), and so do two committed records' scripts (eval/ladder/acceptance-c673738/comparison.txt:58, eval/consistency/ladder-300/checks.txt:31). run_all.py:798 and pool_check.py:164 compare it whole.

Sizes (run 05). Per-frame lines are 92.46% of the ladder report text at 300 frames per pair (308925 bytes, 22960 as committed). Over every frame they are 99.91% (27969051 bytes of text, 1792136 as committed); the rest is 23300 and 26455 bytes. Candidate C1, every score repeated as a §7-style timeline entry, grows the full report to 54462827 bytes, 3498340 compressed. Apple's advanced sample lists 100 segments per variant (run 06) against 36000 frames per 60 fps pair. 51265 vmaf values are written as the integer literal 100, so a schema must type these fields as number, not integer (run 05).

Time base. ref_pts is raw stream time: the advanced sample starts at 10.016666666666667 s (run 04). At EXT-X-DISCONTINUITY the timestamps can restart ('at 1.433367, the time of period A's first', docs/PHASE2_SURVEY.md:47), so PTS alone can't key a timeline. ManifestTag::pts is playlist time, a running sum of EXTINF (src/ManifestParser.cpp:236, :343), while ref_pts is media time; HlsAlign names both (src/HlsAlign.h:35, :117, :168). The 30 fps variants are scored at every other reference frame (ref_index step 2, off_grid_reference 18000), and each reference frame has one ref_pts in every pair that scored it (run 11).

Committed copies are redacted before commit (eval/ladder/pool_check.py:117-118, eval/consistency/ladder_check.py:25-27; e.g. "url": "<ladder>", run 04). A hash of the bytes mirage_vmaf wrote therefore won't match the committed file, which matters for any document that names a ladder report by hash.

Config mechanism. A config setting can be given once (src/VMAFCli.cpp:223-225) and an option once on the command line (:290), so a scripted switch plan, which is a list, needs its own file recorded by path and SHA-256 like config_file (src/VMAFReport.cpp:146-150). mirage_vmaf has no subcommands: an unrecognized argument is an error (src/VMAFCli.cpp:288). The attribution parameters don't affect scores, so putting them in the scoring run's options means rescoring to change them.

Decoder events: a complete ladder report can't carry any today. A receive_frame error ends the input (src/VMAFAnalyzer.cpp:207), and the pair is then reported incomplete (src/VMAFReport.cpp:217-228). avcodec_send_packet's result is ignored (:231), and no key flag or decode-error flag is read (run 14).

Compatibility. Adding top-level keys breaks nothing. Adding keys under pairs[], pooled, ffmpeg_libraries or config_file breaks exact key counts in tests/test_vmaf_report.cpp (:909, :379, :359, :406). Adding keys inside ladder or reference makes run_all's ladder-300 step differ from its committed record (eval/run_all.py:798). Adding per-frame keys makes the acceptance comparison count every frame as changed (comparison.txt:74), and breaks pool_check if the values vary between runs (pool_check.py:156). Renaming model, scaler and similar keys makes every vmafdelta pair FAIL with SETTINGS MISMATCH (vmafdelta.py:1005-1016). The same rename passes silently in ladder_check, where a key missing from both reports compares equal (ABSENT, :71, :310-312), and in pool_check.

Trade-off and recommendation. Option B, a separate session document that names the ladder report by hash, is the agent's recommendation over A (in the ladder report, as §7 lists it) and C (both). Reasons: D-068 scores a ladder once for many sessions; rescoring the full advanced ladder took 1882.86 s (eval/ladder/acceptance-c673738/README.md:20); per-frame data dominates file size; and the existing scripts and tests that compare ladder reports stay valid. B costs a JSON reader in src/, a hash rule that survives redaction, and a difference from §7 to report.
Unit tests for the report, JSON and CLI pass at 75cf6e0: 1368 assertions in 43 test cases (run 09).
open_issues: Does recording per-frame decoder facts in the analyzer (key flags, decode_error_flags, packets the decoder rejects) count as a decode-path change under D-007 and D-068 ('The render and decode paths don't change for it', docs/DECISIONS.md:682)? Option C needs them; B can take keyframes from a demux pass.
How to hash a ladder report when the committed copies are redacted: hash the redacted text, a part redaction doesn't touch, or both.

There is no JSON reader in src/ and no JSON Schema validator in the stdlib-only eval tooling. Checking §7's schema file against reports needs a new dependency, a hand-written validator, or key tests as today.
The timeline's time key across EXT-X-DISCONTINUITY (options T1-T4 in schema.md §3.4) is open, and it decides D-069's ad-boundary test.
The media playlists aren't hashed in the ladder report, so tags read from them later can't be tied to the playlists that were scored.
During a lower-frame-rate variant a session's curve has no score at every other reference frame. What the curve and the sliding baseline do there is open.
The player's session log layout is undecided (D-068), and --net-report leaves out the first-byte time that §3.1 asks for.

§7 and §3 leave open: no session or variant field in timeline entries; pts is a point while §3.1's sources include spans; attributions are a flat list with no grouping by source, no offsets and no detection parameters; the baseline window and statistic aren't defined; there is no rung numbering for 'rung 5 to rung 3'. Options B and C differ from §7's single output.
Does a schema cover only new reports, or also the 12 committed mirage_vmaf layouts?

MEASUREMENT PENDING: the size of a timeline or session document and of per-variant events (nothing is built), the reports of D-069's synthetic ladders, and the number of HTTP requests in a real session.
